title: Frank confident Palace have found turning point after his first win in charge
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutFrank confident Palace have found turning point after his first win in chargeShareThomas Frank has a first Crystal Palace win under his belt, but he now wants one in the Premier League against Hull City on Sunday.Thomas Frank believes his first win in charge of Crystal Palace, against Real Sociedad, could act as a turning point as they return to Premier League action against Hull City.
Frank's first league game in charge was a 3-2 loss to Coventry City, with a late own goal condemning them to a chastening defeat and leaving them bottom of the table.
However, Palace came from behind to beat La Real in the Europa League on Thursday, thanks to goals from Jean-Philippe Mateta and Dwight McNeil.
With the Eagles looking to end a five-game losing run in the league, Frank believes the confidence boost from that victory can spur his side on.
"What I really liked was the belief of the players," he said after the La Real victory. "It is so important to keep doing the right things and keep believing.
"I think it could be [a turning point]. But we need to follow it up, of course, with a good performance against Hull on Sunday. But there were a lot of positives from this game."
Hull got back to winning ways last time out in the Premier League, ending their eight-game wait for a victory with a dramatic 2-0 success over second-placed Brighton.
The Tigers left it late, with Oli McBurnie netting both goals in second-half stoppage time, but Hull are now chasing a first away win in the competition since MD2 against Coventry.
Boss Sergej Jakirovic, however, believes Hull will face a challenge against Palace, who will be more positive after their midweek win.
"Thomas is now in charge; they won their game, which is important for their confidence," he said.
"They can create problems, and we have to be fully concentrating on our task."
Lerma could make his 200th Premier League appearance in this match.
He would be the first Colombian to do so, and the third South American player from outside of Argentina and Brazil, after Antonio Valencia (325) and Nolberto Solano (302).
Tzolakis has both made the most saves (48) and has the best save percentage (81.4%) in the Premier League this season.
It is also the most saves per game (4.4) and the best save ratio by a Hull goalkeeper in a single top-flight campaign.
This is the first meeting between Palace and Hull in any competition since May 2017, a 4-0 win for the Eagles at Selhurst Park that confirmed the Tigers' relegation from the Premier League.
Hull have won just one of their last 13 away games against Palace in all competitions (D5 L7), a 2-0 victory in April 2015 in the Premier League.

However, Palace have lost five consecutive Premier League matches, last enduring a longer losing run in June and July 2020 (seven in a row). The last time they lost more in a row while conceding at least twice was between September and November 2013 (seven).

The Eagles have conceded 58 Premier League goals in 2026, seven more than any other side and their most in a year since 2021 (64). Since and including a 3-1 defeat to Liverpool on April 25, Palace have conceded more goals than any other side in Europe's big five leagues (42).

Meanwhile, Hull are one of only three teams in Europe's big five leagues who are yet to either score or concede more than two goals in a top-flight match this season, along with Lille and Lorient, but given Palace's home advantage, they are favourites to win on Sunday.
